html:
Patria, Minerva and Maria Teresa Mirabal were three sisters who opposed the dictatorship of Rafael Trujillo and were murdered by his agents on 25 November 1960. They were known as Las Mariposas, the butterflies.

They belonged to the underground 14 June Movement, and their husbands were in prison. Trujillo's men stopped their car on a mountain road, beat them to death and staged a crash.

The killings outraged the country and helped bring about Trujillo's assassination six months later. In 1999 the United Nations made 25 November the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women in their memory. Their story is told in the novel In the Time of the Butterflies by Julia Alvarez.
